reviews.comment: ABSOLUTEGOAT

Rating doesn't mean much because the TA matters far more for MEEN 345. The course needs some touching up, because the labs and materials felt less than refined at some points. The lab exams are stupid and don't need to exist, but they aren't hard. Dr. Kim is very accessible by email if ever you need to get into contact with him.

He talks really slow. I had him online, so I could put him at 1.75x speed, but if you take him in person be prepared. He focused too much on derivations instead of example problems. The scope and length of the homework was also very inconsistent, and a few things on the homework weren't even covered in the lecture. Overall he's fine but not good.

Kim is a solid professor, but his voice makes me want to fall asleep. You can't skip lecture, though, since there are a couple of pop quizzes throughout the semester. The homeworks for this class were often very long and tiring to complete. The exams weren't terrible, as he lets you bring a cheat sheet.
He is very attractive
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Kim has very boring lectures, but you can't skip due to random pop quizzes. He grades the exams hard, and it's hard to finish multiple long problems in the 50 minutes given. Some of the exam questions are also edge cases, which you aren't prepared for.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very boring lectures packed with information. There are random in-class quizzes throughout the semester. The exams are in class, meaning a short amount of time and it is very difficult to finish on time. The exam questions are niche and are not emphasized on the homeworks and the grading is harsh. He had typos that wasted time during the exam too.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TA matters more than Kim. His tests were super easy and he made some funny jokes during the final. Extended our formal labs past the deadline so we could do them after the tests both times. Pretty free class overall.

Kim is not the greatest studio professor to have for capstone. He requires weekly presentations, which are not too bad but he does not seem to care too much about the project and really only cares about administrative information. Overall not bad but its like talking to a wall

In 345 you don't really interact with him unless he leads your section of fluid lab. Most people only interact with the TA so I'm basing my rating pretty much just on the exams that we had to take. Final was easy to prepare for and take, the first exam was okay, but doable. He's aight, TAs carry more weight on your grade than Haejune

Haejune Kim is a decent professor. You can tell he cares about his students, but his lectures are some of the worst I've been to. Good material, but even in 50 min he makes them tedious, long, and monotoned. Tests are pretty difficult, but for my class the grading was very fair. Great guy, you can just tell he doesn't want to teach thermo

Took this class with him over the summer. He was a good choice and was very clear and organized in his prerecorded lectures. He made thermodynamics more interesting and the concepts easy to grasp. The last two exams had 10 extra credit bonus points added to them. I wish I took him in the spring instead of Yu so I wouldn't have had to q-drop.
Online labs stink in the sense of being able to pay attention. It's a lot of work with lab reports, postlab/prelab, midterm, and final. But its pretty easy to do well so long as you do all the work.

Just don't take him please for your own sake. Video lectures are well prepared yet the test is nowhere near close to homework or the book. You'll definitely understand the concepts but you'll get confused on the test on how to apply what you have learned. Dr. Kim is really nice yet he has a thick accent which makes it hard to focus.

For any thermo section final and tests are pretty heavy in grade, but prof Kims lectures were informative and tests were very similar to the homework and quizzes. He had practice exams and an exam review which was very helpful. Lecture videos are short and informative, he gets to what you need to know and shows how to use equations/concepts

He is absolutely one of the worst profs you can take. I received a B, but to do so required more work than any other class Ive taken at TAMU. His final was outright stupid. An extra hour was needed and so was a curve, yet there was none. Youre better off dropping out than taking Kim.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pretty sure hes a robot. Do not take if you want to learn thermodynamics. Otherwise just read the textbook, thats all he does anyways.

Took this class over the Summer. The semester was going fine until the final which was 30% of the grade and he made it the hardest final on planet earth, every test of was felt like I needed 30 mins more to complete it but the final felt like I need 3 more hours. The avg was a F on the final and there are no curves. So get ready to take an L.

By far one of the most inconsistent professors I had. Took back an A he gave me on exam 2 and turned it into a a B. Then grades finals giving almost no partial credit like he gave on the first exam. He mentions a curve then will answer no questions about it and claims he no longer is giving a curve. DO NOT TAKE, INCONSISTENT!!!
Dudes a real great fella. A certified beauty, provides a solid full send every lecture.

Take Dr. Kim for Thermodynamics. Bits and pieces of his lectures, homework, and suggested problems are on the exam with numbers changed. Easy to get an A so long as you follow those 3 things and understand what's going on. If you want more in-depth understanding, then the book is a good resource.

Dr. Kim is the best to have for Thermodynamics hands down. He gives clear expectations for exams. Follow his lectures and read sections in the book that pertain to them and there will be no problems to having an A. Very straight forward, listens to student feedback, and although dry most times, entertaining lectures with props he brings for demos.

Dr. Kim has well prepped and interesting lectures. He explains the material well to students. He gives online quizzes mostly and his quizzes mirror his exams. Homework does more than enough to prepare you for each exam as well. Hes well prepped to keep us entertained. He even brought a thermal laser to class and explained how it worked.
If you study each lab for one hour apiece, you will do fine on the tests.

Dr. Kim is a super nice guy and a great prof! I took heat transfer over the summer online, and as long as you watch all the lectures and practice the in class examples as well as the homework the tests were pretty easy. I would definitely take him again.
